planning.role: Source research, visual plan, narration and companion prose

cover.subject: Common octopus
cover.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: isolated animal artwork for an O'RLY parody technical-book cover. Draw one anatomically plausible common octopus in fine nineteenth-century natural-history copperplate engraving style, dark charcoal ink, precise crosshatching and stippling, all eight curling arms fully visible, graceful compact composition, intelligent eye. Subject occupies about 75 percent of a square canvas. Background must be a perfectly uniform pure white #FFFFFF field edge to edge, no tan, cream, ivory, paper texture, vignette, horizon, scene, rocks, seaweed, props or shadow. The animal is the only content. Absolutely no letters, words, numbers, logos, borders, banners or watermarks. This is animal art only, not a rendered book.
edits: Preserve the octopus engraving and replace empty background with solid #FFFFFF.
Extract the same engraving as a transparent cutout, preserving all ink detail and white highlights, for exact-white flattening.
cover.preparation: Flattened ImageGen cutout onto #FFFFFF, retained full PNG locally, and converted to a 512px-wide WebP using generator/cover.mjs.
cover.validation: Visually checked the final WebP: one full animal, no lettering, no scene or frame. Sampled PNG background pixels are RGB 255,255,255.

accuracy.evidence: Independent audit traced all 40 captions to the pinned source. The three narration corrections and corresponding prose corrections are active. All 40 published sources.json claim texts match the reviewed narration. Source-sensitive visual corrections are clear.

depth.evidence: Explains snapshot namespaces, process-generation identity, stable versus mutable text, geometry tie-breaking, partial/drill completeness, auto-wait and lease ordering, delivery/retry semantics, verification scope, and retained-owner expiry.
depth.limits: A focused command/identity explainer, not a complete platform/API reference.

story.evidence: Observe-act-observe introduces the question of whether an old observation can safely address a live target. Identity, dispatch gates, and host lifecycle answer it before the closing loop returns responsibility to the agent.
story.limits: The arc is coherent but primarily explanatory; no claim of exceptional dramatic storytelling.

visual.evidence: Reviewed revised contact sheets, relevant full frames, and final cards. The picture now exposes partial boundaries, complete-before-replacement drill state, mutable-role exclusions, geometry disambiguation, unresolved refusal, leased re-resolution, and readback. All material punch-list findings are resolved; 50 forward/reverse samples match with zero browser errors, clipping, or caption overlap.
visual.limits: Source-clock stills, deterministic sampling, four production previews, and mobile blog screenshots were inspected. Automated reader/blog rendering checks pass. This is not continuous perceptual audio/visual playback.

sync.evidence: Narration log records 40 exact authored captions verified before synthesis. Manifest has 10 strictly increasing cue starts per chapter; all cue intervals are positive and inside chapter duration. Audio QA reports duration agreement and no decode errors. Deterministic scene sampling passes. Production runtime now confirms 80 exact caption seeks and four advancing playback clocks.
sync.limits: Provisional timing-data score, capped per docs/book-quality.md. Automated reader caption/clock checks and blog runtime checks pass. No perceptual narrated watching was performed; the automated playback check was muted, and no claim is made that motion was heard to land on words.

sound.evidence: All four MP3 files decode according to audio-qa.json. Chapter average rates are 162.89, 147.08, 151.20, and 156.43 words/minute, within the rubric 110–170 range. Spoken captions mostly use prose rather than raw ref tokens. No music is configured in the manifest.
sound.limits: No listening performed. Voice quality, pronunciation, prosody, audible transitions, clipping/noise, and local delivery pace are unverified. MP3 decoding and average word rates do not establish perceptual quality.

curiosity.evidence: The ref-as-observation mental model, geometry as corroborating evidence, uncertain delivery versus safe retry, and persistent native owner make concrete reasons to inspect the code.
curiosity.limits: An editorial assessment, not measured audience engagement.

limitations: No perceptual watching or listening was performed. Sync and sound are provisional scores from script, cue timing, still frames, and technical audio reports, within the documented 6.5–7.5 cap.

Production build, four-chapter verification, 80 exact caption seeks, four advancing playback clocks, eight silent blog SVG sections, and mobile portrait/landscape visibility/overflow checks pass. These automated checks do not replace perceptual watching/listening.
Source correctness was assessed against the pinned implementation, docs, and test definitions; this is not a live cross-platform behavior certification.
Average chapter speaking rates and successful decoding do not establish pronunciation, prosody, audible quality, or moment-to-moment pacing.
Source behavior is pinned to the cited revision; this book does not claim to test live native automation on all supported operating systems.
No subjective listening review was possible. Audio judgments use the script, exact alignment, duration, and measured playback behavior.
